notes: Libretto by Lorenzo Da Ponte (1787). Words follow the Schirmer vocal score's spelling and punctuation where the libretto differs: Leporello sings "colla bella" (libretto: con la bella), "Sta a veder" (Sta'), "sò" and "quà", and "o ciel!" in bar 85; his aside "(Potessi almeno di quà partir!)" keeps the print's brackets. Anna's "Scellerato!" and the Commendatore's "battiti" / "Battiti!" keep the print's single consonant; the IPA is as sung (ʃel.leˈra.to, ˈbat.ti.ti). Giovanni sings "già cade" (libretto: cadde) and "affannoso" (libretto: affannosa); in bar 181 affannoso, e and the a- of agonizzante share one note. Lines are repeated as the score repeats them, each repeat its own phrase. IPA, word meanings and translations were drafted for this app (S02) and the IPA was checked against Castel. IPA follows sung Italian conventions: stressed syllable marked, elisions (two words on one note in the score) joined with ‿, open e/o as ɛ/ɔ. Translation literal, for meaning.
